minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Agency,
  Community Development Financing Authority,
  Public Improvement Corporation,
  and Library Board of Trustees*

  May 3, 2010

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Agency, the Community
Development Financing Authority, the Public Improvement Corporation, and the Library Board
of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Kelley at 5:05
p.m., on May 3, 2010, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on April 30, 2020, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the
Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Ledesma
  Council Member Schlicht
  Council Member Ury
  Mayor Pro Tem Leckness (arrived at 5:08 p.m.)
  Mayor Kelley

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  Irwin B. Bornstein, Assistant City Manager/Director of Admin. Services
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Kelley

INVOCATION: Council Member Ledesma

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with City Attorney Concerning One matter of Existing Litigation
  Pursuant to Government Code Section 54956.9(a). The Litigation is City of Mission

City Council Minutes  1  May 3, 2010
   Viejo v. CUSD, Case No. 00180049; Companion Case, Rancho Santa Margarita v.
  CUSD, Case No. 00207543

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:07 p.m., Mayor Kelley recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City
Council reconvened at 6:04 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that for Closed Session Item CS1, the Council received an
update and gave instruction to staff but there was no reportable action.

PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Proclaim May 2010 as Water Awareness Month

  Mayor Kelley presented Proclamations to Scott Goldman, Vice President of El Toro
  Water District and Charley Wilson, Vice President of Santa Margarita Water District.
  Moulton Niguel Water District was not in attendance but a Proclamation will be
  provided.

P2.  Presentation by the Building Industry Association of Orange County (BIA)

  The City Council received a presentation entitled “The BIA Gives Back” from Dave
  Bartlett, President, and Jill Cagle, Public Affairs Director for the BIA.

P3.  Presentation of Awards Received for the City’s 2009-11 Budget Document and 2009
  Comprehensive Annual Financial Report from the Government Finance Officers
  Association of the United States and Canada.

  Mayor Kelley received the awards.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Joyce Sawaya, Barbara Harris, and Alice Alhman, Members of the Casta del Sol Vegetable
Garden Club, M.V.: thanked Waste Management for providing and delivering compost for their
vegetable gardens. The compost helps them conserve water, share vegetables with the
community, and the gardeners were able to donate extra compost and volunteer with the planting
event at Arts Alive.

Larry Mauer, Member of the Friends of the Library Board of Directors, M.V.: announced that
the library book store generates $125,000 a year and the Board recently voted to give $50,000 in

City Council Minutes  2  May 3, 2010
 support of the 2010 Readers’ Festival. He discussed library patron’s individual stories of success
and thanked Library Director Valerie Maginnis for her dedication.

Joyce Saltzgiver, M.V.: stated that residents of Casta del Sol have no complaints about their trash
service and she expressed support for a continued contract with Waste Management. Mrs.
Saltzgiver asked the Council to consider eliminating the planned cut-through on Casta del Sol
Drive and she also asked for rejection of Council Member Schlicht’s claim for mileage and
parking reimbursement (item #17).

Claudia and Milton Bradford, M.V.: asked the City Council to support their request for an
unusual animal license in order to house a miniature horse in their back yard.

Marlene Gerloff, M.V.: asked the City Council to postpone the decision on the usage of the
Potocki Center (agenda item #13) because the Heritage Committee would like time to prepare a
presentation and proposal for a Mission Viejo Cultural Arts Center at that location.

Geoff Willis, Co-Chair of the No on D Committee, M.V.: discussed the origins of Measure D
and his opposition to the measure.

Wendy Bucknum, M.V.: representing the Chamber of Commerce, she stated that Measure D
hurts small businesses because they would be forced to fund expensive elections. For more
information on fighting the Measure, she encouraged residents to visit
ww.protectmissionviejo.com.

Dan Avery, M.V.: expressed support for Waste Management and stated that they provide
excellent service to the residents of Mission Viejo. He also noted that defenders of Measure D
have trouble telling voters why they should support the measure and he encouraged residents to
reject it on June 8th.

Donna Varner, M.V.: stated that the members of No on Measure D are Mission Viejo residents
who feel that if approved, the measure will be a disaster for the city and will discourage
businesses and residents from coming to Mission Viejo.

Kime Goodrum, M.V.: asked the city to post the names of the individuals who abuse the Public
Records Act process and summarize how much these requests have cost the city.

Helen Workun, M.V.: encouraged residents of Mission Viejo to vote no on Measure D.

Dennis O’Connor, Co-Chair of No on Measure D, M.V.: stated that he gets many requests from
residents who want to know how they can help defeat Measure D.

Christopher Sullivan, Co-Artistic Director of the Modjeska Playhouse: announced that Modjeska
Playhouse intends to establish a permanent theater space in Saddleback Valley and he invited the
Council and residents to a performance of "The Frog Prince" on May 15 and 16, 2010.

City Council Minutes  3  May 3, 2010
 Nancy Cho, M.V.: thanked the City Council Members for attending the dedication of the
Saddleback College Veterans Memorial. She echoed opposition to Measure D and stated that
new businesses don’t need extra steps and expenses if they want to come to Mission Viejo.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 2, 3 and 5 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion.

Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Council Member Ledesma, to approve the
Consent Calendar as described below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Ledesma, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said
  titles which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title
  and further reading waived.

4.  Check Register dated April 16, 2010, in the amount of $624,769.57

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

6.  Amendment to the City of Mission Viejo Housing Rehabilitation Program

  Adopted Resolution 10-18 Approving an Amendment to the City of Mission Viejo
  Housing Rehabilitation Program Rules and Regulations to Increase the Maximum Award
  Amount by $5000, from $25,000 to $30,000.

7.  2010 Residential Resurfacing-Community Development Block Grant (CIP 838)

  Approved the bid specifications and authorized staff to advertise for construction bids for
  the subject project, contingent upon approval of the Fiscal Year 2010-2011 CDBG
  Action Plan.

8.  Oso Creek Restoration and Protection Project (CIP 207)-Montanoso Recreation
  Center Bio-Swale Construction Award

City Council Minutes  4  May 3, 2010
   (1) Rejected the bid from Rock Bottom, Inc., as being unresponsive; and (2) awarded the
  construction contract in the amount of $76,712.00 to Atlas Engineering Company for the
  subject project.

Item 13 was taken out of order.

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, AND COMMITTEE REPORTS

13.  Use Agreement with Outta Bounds Events for use of the Thomas R. Potocki Center
  for Youth Activities

  Community Services Manager Steve Bell presented the staff report.

  The following spoke in support of the Outta Bounds programs and activities: Anita
  Armstrong, M.V.; Iris Disher, M.V.; Robin Rangel, M.V.; Ken Harrison, M.V.;
  Stephanie Cristus, M.V.; John Covert, Ladera Ranch; Julie Raff, M.V.; Carl Raff, M.V.;
  Jenny Raff, M.V.; Gretchen Malcolm, San Juan Capistrano; Catherine Milovich, Rancho
  Santa Margarita; Julia Oien, M.V.; Linda and Christopher Orem, M.V.; and Scott
  Ramirez, M.V.

  The following spoke in support of an Arts Center at the Potocki Complex: George
  Katzenberger, Irvine; and Helen Workun, M.V.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Leckness, seconded by Mayor Kelley, to (1) direct staff
  to issue a Request for Proposals to organizations for use of the Thomas R. Potocki
  Center, and (2) in the interim approve the Use Agreement with Outta Bounds Events
  (A10-12) for use of the Thomas R. Potocki Center for youth activities during summer
  2010 and the 2010-11 school year.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Ledesma, and Schlicht
  NOES:  Ury
  ABSENT: None

RECESS

At the hour 8:24 p.m., Mayor Kelley declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at 8:35
p.m., with all five City Council Members present.

PUBLIC HEARINGS

9.  Proposed 2010-2014 Implementation Plan for the Community Development Project
  Area

City Council Minutes  5  May 3, 2010
   Special Counsel Celeste Brady, Stradling Yocca Carlson & Rauth, presented the staff
  report.

  Mayor Kelley opened the public hearing at 8:43 p.m.

  Joe Hotlzman, M.V.: asked what the CDA’s debt load is.

  At the hour of 8:44 p.m., Mayor Kelley closed the public hearing.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Council Member Ledesma, to adopt
  CDA Resolution 10-03 Approving the 2010-2014 Implementation Plan for the
  Community Development Project Area Pursuant to Section 33490 of the Community
  Redevelopment Law and Making Certain Findings in Connection Therewith.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Ledesma, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

10.  Appeal of Planned Development Permit PDP2009-221 Filed by Council Member
  Cathy Schlicht of the Planning and Transportation Commission’s February 8, 2010
  Approval of a City Initiated Petition Submitted by the City of Mission Viejo
  Recreation and Community Services Department for the Marguerite Tennis,
  Aquatics, and Recreation Center Complex Renovation and Expansion Project at
  23840 Marguerite Parkway, in the R (Recreation) and RPD 6.5 (Residential
  Planned Development) Zones

  Director of Community Development Chuck Wilson presented the staff report.

  At the hour of 9:12 p.m., Mayor Kelley opened the public hearing.

  The following spoke in opposition to the appeal and in support of the improvements to
  the Marguerite Tennis Center: Wil Garcia, M.V.; Rolland Graham, M.V.; Kime
  Goodrum, M.V.; Bob Bruchmann, M.V.; Tom Teichmann, M.V.; Wendy Bucknum,
  M.V.; Bob Howe, M.V.; Rick Sandzimier, M.V.

  The following requested that the City conduct a full Environmental Impact Report for the
  proposed project and/or expressed concern about the cost of the project: Tina Bach, M.V.
  and Harry Lenczyk, M.V.

  The following presented written comments in favor of the Tennis Center expansion
  project: Lori Seely, M.V. and Julie Farrow, M.V.

City Council Minutes  6  May 3, 2010
   Mayor Kelley closed the public hearing at 9:47 p.m.

  Motion made by Council Member Ledesma, seconded by Council Member Ury, to (1)
  adopt Resolution 10-19 Denying the Appeal and Adopting a Mitigated Negative
  Declaration for Planned Development Permit PDP2009-221, Being a City-Initiated
  Petition for the Marguerite Tennis, Aquatics, and Recreation Center Complex Renovation
  and Expansion Project at 23840 Marguerite Parkway, in the R (Recreation) and RPD 6.5
  (Residential Planned Development) Zones; (2) adopt a Mitigated Negative Declaration
  declaring that Planned Development Permit PDP2009-221 will not have a significant
  effect on the environment based on the revisions made to the project that mitigate or
  avoid the potential significant effects on the environment that may otherwise occur; (3)
  review and confirm that the proposed construction project currently under design is
  consistent with the Master Plan and attendant environmental documentation; and (4)
  approve the Fourth Amendment with Hodge & Associates(A09-20D) for additional
  environmental consulting services in the amount of $1,275.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Ledesma, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT: None

OLD BUSINESS

11.  Integrated Solid Waste Management Services Agreement

  Joe Sloan and Enrique Vazquez, Sloan Vazquez Consulting, LLC, presented the report
  and outlined the methodology behind the evaluation of the four proposals and described
  how they arrived at the recommendation.

  The following discussed their company’s proposal and answered questions of the City
  Council: Brett Barbre, Athens Services; Dean Ruffridge, CR&R; Jason Rush and Judith
  Ware, Ware Disposal; and David Ross, Waste Management of Orange County.

  Max Carter, Executive Director, Orange County Conservation Corps, M.V.: discussed
  Waste Management’s efforts to help improve their program for at-risk young adults.

  Joe Holtzman, M.V.: expressed appreciation for the job that Sloan Vazquez has done
  with the assessment and noted the he will come back and comment on the pro forma
  aspect of the analysis at the next opportunity.

  Tefere Gebre, Orange: discussed the retention of sanitation workers and noted that the
  truck drivers and employees of Waste Management are a commodity that should be
  recognized and retained.

City Council Minutes  7  May 3, 2010
   Doug Wooley, Community Development Manager for Goodwill of Orange County,
  Laguna Niguel: discussed their partnership with Waste Management which helps
  Goodwill fulfill their mission to assist people with disabilities. In doing so, they provide
  an opportunity for these individuals to achieve personal and economic independence and
  the partnership program has received national recognition.

  The following presented written comments in favor of a contract with Waste
  Management: Debbie Lewandowski, M.V. and Anna T. Boyce, M.V.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Leckness, to
  continue this item to the next City Council Meeting.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Ledesma, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, AND COMMITTEE REPORTS (Continued)

By consensus, the City Council continued these items to the next meeting.

14.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

15.  Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report

16.  San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

2.  City Council Minutes

  Council Member Schlicht stated that the Minutes should reflect the discussion regarding
  Hodge and Associates' contract. The consultants attended just one public hearing yet
  their contract required attendance at two public hearings (page 6, item 8).

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Kelley, to approve the
  Minutes for the Regular City Council Meeting of April 19, 2010, as presented.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Ledesma, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None

City Council Minutes  8  May 3, 2010
   ABSENT: None

3.  Check Register dated April 9, 2010, in the amount of $612,972.96

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Kelley, to ratify the
  accompanying check register.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Ledesma, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

5.  Draft Consolidated Plan for Fiscal Year (FY) 2010-2014 and Draft Annual Action
  Plan for FY 2010-2011 Detailing City’s Proposed Use of Community Development
  Block Grant (CDBG) Funds

  Council Member Schlicht noted that there is a statement in the agenda report which says
  flood areas are buildable but it costs more to build in those zones.

  The following presented a written comment thanking the City Council for supporting
  Toby's House: Jazquelyn Flora, Toby's House, Santa Ana.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Ury, to adopt
  Resolution 10-17 Approving the City's Draft Consolidated Plan for Fiscal Year (FY)
  2010-2014 and Draft Annual Action Plan for FY 2010-2011 Detailing City’s Proposed
  use of Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) Funds and Authorizing
  Submission of Such Plans to the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development
  (HUD).

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Ledesma, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

NEW BUSINESS

12.  Truck Weight Limit Restrictions

  By consensus, the City Council continued this item to the next meeting.

STAFF REPORTS

City Council Minutes  9  May 3, 2010
 City Manager’s Report

17.  Consideration of Cathy Schlicht’s request for reimbursement of travel and parking
  expenses incurred in association with her attendance in Orange County Superior
  Court in the matter of Cathy Schlicht, City Council Member of the City of Mission
  Viejo v. Karen Hamman, City Clerk of the City of Mission Viejo, and Neal Kelley,
  Orange County Registrar of Voters, Case No. 00352765

  City Manager Dennis Wilberg presented the staff report.

  Bob Bruchmann, M.V.: stated that it cost the City $40,000 to defend an unnecessary
  lawsuit filed by Council Member Schlicht and therefore, he is opposed to the idea of
  reimbursing her for her travel to the court house.

  Motion was made by Council Member Schlicht to approve the reimbursement request
  from Council Member Schlicht for travel and parking expenses incurred in association
  with her attendance in Orange County Superior Court.

  The motion died for lack of a second.

18.  Possible Professional Sports Opportunity

  City Manager Wilberg advised the Council that staff has received a proposal to bring a
  minor league baseball stadium to Mission Viejo. The individuals who presented the
  proposal have requested that the agenda item be continued to a date uncertain.

City Attorney’s Report

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS

19.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as
  presented in the staff report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the
  public record.

Council Member Ledesma

Council Member Schlicht

20.  Transparency in Government

  Due to the late hour, Council Member Schlicht announced that she would like to continue
  this item to the next City Council Meeting.

City Council Minutes  10  May 3, 2010
 Council Member Ury

Mayor Pro Tem Leckness

Mayor Kelley

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 12:29 a.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this
session, Mayor Kelley adjourned the meeting in memory of Jim Gilleran to Monday, May 17,
2010, at 5:00 p.m.

__________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of May 17, 2010

City Council Minutes  11  May 3, 2010
